analysis.title: Really Market Now Implying Zero Earnings Growth
key_insights: The week's selloff triggered one of the sharpest positioning resets in years. Hedge funds cut exposure aggressively and broader equity positioning moved to underweight.
Barclays estimates the latest selloff produced the largest single-day selling requirement from leveraged ETF rebalancing on record.
Goldman reports hedge funds sold AI stocks at their fastest pace in more than five years. On a rolling 20-day basis, selling hit three standard deviations below normal.
Deutsche Bank's measure of megacap growth and technology positioning fell to the 7th percentile of its historical range.
DB says tech positioning is in line with a sharp deceleration, outright negative growth and large estimate cuts.
JPM reports hedge-fund net leverage fell another 4% last week, approaching 12-month lows. Equity long/short net exposure is at three-year lows.
Goldman reports US fundamental long/short gross leverage fell 8.7 points in one week, the largest weekly reduction since the March 2020 Covid crash.
Goldman reports US fundamental long/short net leverage fell 3.7 points last week, the largest decline since Liberation Day, leaving it at the 0th percentile of its five-year range.

JPM reports global hedge-fund momentum exposure fell toward three-year lows. With positioning near neutral and the six-month positioning/price indicator near its summer lows, the unwind may be nearing exhaustion.
Deutsche Bank says its equity positioning measure fell to an underweight, one of the biggest weekly drops in positioning.

DB finds overall equity positioning is at levels historically consistent with zero earnings growth, while actual earnings remain firmly positive. The open question is whether earnings fall to positioning or positioning rises to earnings.
